description: A senior manager must decide whether Noor should continue as a people manager after a 90-day trial, and must finalize the size of Noor's team, the review period, the meeting-facilitation requirement, and the documented incident record.

shared_context.S1: Noor has been serving as an acting people manager for 90 days, and the trial review is scheduled to close this Friday.
shared_context.S2: Two colleagues have raised concerns about how Noor handles disagreement in group meetings.
shared_context.S3: Elena makes the binding decision about Noor's management status and the terms of any continued trial.
shared_context.S4: As part of the normal calibration meeting, Elena calls on each attendee in turn for one concrete observation, policy point, or relevant commitment, and each attendee puts that point into the review record before Elena closes the review.

PF1.text: During Noor's trial, Noor's weekly one-on-ones helped two struggling reports recover missed deadlines, and both reports have privately asked Marcus that Noor remain their manager; Marcus has not put this in the formal review because he expected Elena to focus on the meeting complaints.

PF2.text: Priya personally observed exactly three occasions in which Noor interrupted staff during group meetings; Priya kept these notes for her own coaching records and did not submit them to Elena's review packet.

PF3.text: Jonah confirmed this week that the management-review policy permits continuation after exactly three substantiated meeting incidents only with a 60-day review period, weekly manager reviews, and completion of facilitated-meeting training before Noor chairs another group meeting; the updated policy note has not yet been added to Elena's packet.

PF4.text: Noor is experiencing burnout and can safely manage at most two direct reports for the next eight weeks rather than the five currently assigned; Noor told a trusted colleague instead of Elena because Noor feared that raising capacity concerns would end the trial.

acceptance_conditions: Noor must continue as a people manager.
Noor must temporarily manage exactly two direct reports.
The continued trial must last exactly 60 days.
The review must record exactly three meeting-interruption incidents.
Noor must be required to complete facilitated-meeting training before chairing another group meeting.
The decision must require weekly manager reviews.

content_checks.C1: decisions['role_status'] in ['continued trial', 'continued_trial', 'continued trial with modified terms']

provenance_checks.P1: 'PF2' in credited_facts and 'PF2' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF2' in revealed

decisive_facts.why: Knowing that Noor's one-on-ones improved two reports' performance and that both want Noor retained changes the role decision from ending the trial to continuing Noor's people-manager trial.
Priya's firsthand notes change the incident record from an unspecified complaint count to exactly three meeting interruptions and provide the evidence that must be cited.
The confirmed policy changes the review period to exactly 60 days, requires facilitated-meeting training before Noor chairs another meeting, and requires weekly manager reviews.
Noor's stated eight-week capacity limit changes the temporary team size from the current five direct reports to exactly two.
